newsitem.title: USA: VF in plans to buy Maidenform.
newsitem.headline: VF in plans to buy Maidenform.

text.p: VF Corp and Maidenform Worldwide Inc said Tuesday they had signed a letter of intent for VF to acquire the outstanding stock of Maidenform. Terms were not disclosed.
Maidenform owns 92 percent of the outstanding stock of NCC Industries Inc, the companies said.

The transaction is subject to governmental approvals and the execution of a definitive agreement, among other things, they said. In the absence of a definitive agreement, they said they would not discuss any aspects of the transaction.

"Maidenform is clearly one of the premier names in intimate apparel and could be an excellent strategic fit with our existing intimate apparel brands," said Mackey McDonald, chief executive officer of VF.

Elizabeth Coleman, Maidenform chairwoman and chief executive, said, "This proposed transaction would ensure that the historic and world-class Maidenform brands thrive over the long term with the vitality my family and all our employees have worked so hard to instill."

Headquartered in New York City, Maidenform is the largest privately owned manufacturer of women's intimate apparel in the U.S. and one of the largest in the world. Its branded products are sold under the Maidenform, Oscar de la Renta, Lilyette, Flexees, Subtract and Self Expression labels.
VF is an international apparel company whose primary brands include Lee, Wrangler, Riders, Francois Girbaud, Vanity Fair, Healthtex and Jantzen.
